transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Thanks. Well, I'm here because... it's getting really bad at work. I'm a barber, and I've gotten to the point where I will do almost anything to avoid using a straight razor. I'll switch clients with my coworkers, or I'll tell a customer the blade is missing, or I'll just hide it in my drawer. And if I absolutely can't get out of it... I'm just shaking through the whole shave. It's becoming a real problem.
What are you most afraid might happen when you have to use the straight razor?

I know it’s just a tool. I mean, I trained with it, and I can use clippers or shears all day without a second thought. But... when that straight razor is sitting open at my station, it just feels like I’m about to hurt somebody. Or... or cut myself badly. It's just this overwhelming feeling that something terrible is going to happen with it.
Are you afraid that you might lose control and deliberately hurt someone, or are you worried that your hand will slip and cause an accident?

I'm... I'm not really sure, honestly. I definitely don't want to hurt anyone on purpose, so I don't think it's that. But I also don't really sit there picturing my hand slipping, either. 

It's just... I don't know. When the blade is open, I just get this huge wave of panic. I haven't really noticed a specific thought about exactly how it would happen, or who is to blame... it just feels like something terrible is going to happen the second I pick it up.
How long have you been dealing with this fear of using a straight razor?

It's been going on for about 11 months now. It basically started right around the time I was getting into some arguments with the shop owner... we were clashing over this straight-razor shave package he wanted to push at the shop. Ever since those arguments started, this whole fear just kind of set in.

inference_history.note: Patient presents with marked fear, avoidance, and tremor when required to use a straight razor at work. Differential includes specific phobia (fear of sharp objects), obsessive-compulsive disorder (harm obsessions), social anxiety disorder (performance anxiety / fear of shaking in front of clients), and generalized anxiety disorder.
